column5: For peace in all of Alestia, all they had to do was prevail.{w}\nAs the crowd thins out, they press their backs against one another.{w}\nThe enemies may be swinging their swords, but they landed no hits.
column6: 为了全阿莱斯蒂亚的和平，他们只需取胜便可。{w}\n人群渐渐稀疏，他们背靠着背，彼此支撑。{w}\n敌人或许挥剑猛砍，却一剑未中。

column5: So {i}this{/i} is what I was meant to do...
column6: 原来{i}这{/i}就是我的使命……

column5: Huh...?
Gryz swings his hammer, taking out ten more.{w}\nThen, seconds later, they're back to back once again.
column6: 格瑞兹挥动战锤，又干掉了十个。{w}\n几秒后，他们再度背靠着背。

column5: Back in Mazeo, I was ready to throw my life away.\nYou know, to atone for what I did in The Triumvirate's name?\nI'm glad that I didn't — I was meant to end {i}them{/i}, not myself.
column6: 当初在马泽奥，我已准备好舍弃自己的性命。\n你知道的，为以三人执政团之名所做的事赎罪吧？\n幸好我没有——我注定要终结{i}他们{/i}，而不是我自己。

column5: Pro smiles at his ally.
column6: 普洛对战友露出微笑。

column5: I'm glad you made the right choice, then.
column6: 那我很高兴你做出了正确的选择。

column5: He lunges forward, continuing to kill the suits of armor.{w}\nGryz scoffs, a wide smile appearing on his face as he fights.
column6: 他向前猛冲，继续斩杀那些空甲。{w}\n格瑞兹嗤笑一声，战斗的脸上绽开大大的笑容。

column5: No — not me.\nIt's all thanks to [firstname].
column6: 不——不是我。\n这全靠[firstname]。

column5: The battle continues, but the enemy stood no chance.{w}\nThey were killing the suits faster than they entered the room.{w}\nAnd after what seemed like an eternity, they entered no more.
column6: 战斗仍在继续，但敌人毫无胜算。{w}\n他们斩杀空甲的速度，比敌人涌入房间还快。{w}\n仿佛过了永恒那么久，终于再无空甲进来了。

column5: Pro falls to his knees, struggling to catch his breath.{w}\nEven Gryz seems winded, as well. What a thrilling dance that was.{w}\nHowever, as they learn moments later, it's not yet come to an end.
column6: 普洛双膝跪地，拼命喘着气。{w}\n连格瑞兹似乎也气喘吁吁。真是一场惊心动魄的共舞。{w}\n然而，片刻之后他们才明白，这一切尚未结束。

column5: Another group of hordes starts making its way into the large hallway.{w}\nThey laugh. Of course this wouldn't be as easy as they thought.{w}\nCharging into the crowd again, the fight continues, almost endless.
column6: 又一群敌潮开始涌入宽阔的走廊。{w}\n他们笑了。这事当然不会如他们想的那么轻松。{w}\n他们再次冲入人群，战斗继续，仿佛永无止境。

column5: There's too many of them...!\nWe need to do something, and fast!
column6: 他们人太多了……！\n我们必须做点什么，而且要快！

column5: There's nothing we can do!\nJust stand your ground. Keep fighting!
column6: 我们别无他法！\n就守住阵地。继续战斗！

column5: The swings and stabs become weaker with each passing moment.{w}\nWhat was once a certain victory is now falling apart in the face of exertion.{w}\nBut they don't give up. \"Never accept defeat, not until the very end.\"
column6: 每一次挥砍与突刺，都随着时间流逝愈发无力。{w}\n曾笃定的胜利，如今在疲惫面前土崩瓦解。{w}\n但他们不肯放弃。“永不认输，直到最后一刻。”

column5: That was the first rule of any good gambler.{w}\nAnd with their lives as chips on the table, they continued to play;{w}\nThe floor becoming a sea of white and gold in the wake of their rage.
column6: 这是任何好赌徒的第一条准则。{w}\n他们把性命当作桌上的筹码，继续赌下去；{w}\n在他们的怒火之后，地面化作一片白金之海。

column5: All they had to do was pray that they didn't drown in it.{w}\nAs their strength dwindled, they kept fighting, never giving up.{w}\nThat determination saw them through, right to the bitter end.
column6: 他们所能做的，只是祈祷自己不会溺毙其中。{w}\n气力渐渐耗尽，他们仍战斗不休，绝不放弃。{w}\n正是这份决心支撑他们挺到最后，直到苦痛的终点。

column5: Eventually, Pro's path leads him to a massive dining hall.{w}\nHowever, much to his surprise, it also doubles as a dead-end.{w}\nHe examines his surroundings, looking for somewhere to escape.
column6: 最终，普洛的路通向一间巨大的宴会厅。{w}\n然而令他大感意外的是，这里同时也是条死路。{w}\n他打量四周，寻找可以逃脱的地方。

column5: Damn it! There's nowhere to go.
column6: 该死！无路可逃了。

column5: With each passing second, The Honor Guard grows closer.{w}\nIn a panic, Pro grabs a couple knives from the table. Daggers.{w}\nHe hadn't planned to fight, but it appears that he had no choice.
column6: 每一秒过去，荣誉卫队都越来越近。{w}\n惊慌之中，普洛从桌上抓起几把刀。是匕首。{w}\n他本没打算战斗，但看来已别无选择。

column5: The windows here were iron bars, rather than stained glass.{w}\nIt almost makes it seem as if this room is a prison. How fitting.{w}\nHe takes a deep breath, and waits for the suits to enter the room.
column6: 这里的窗户装着铁栅，而非彩绘玻璃。{w}\n这几乎让房间显得像座牢房。倒也贴切。{w}\n他深吸一口气，等待空甲进入房间。

column5: But when they do, he's shocked. There's far more than before.{w}\nAs if they gathered up several hordes to follow him in pursuit.{w}\nBoth a bad sign, and a good sign. His distraction really worked.
column6: 可当它们进来时，他震惊了。数量远胜从前。{w}\n仿佛它们聚拢了好几群敌潮来追捕他。{w}\n这既是坏兆头，也是好兆头。他的牵制确实奏效了。

column5: Heh — is that all you could bring...?\nI thought you'd be giving me a challenge.
column6: 呵——你们就只带得来这些……？\n我还以为你们能给我点挑战。

column5: He jumps ontop of the table, giving him a height advantage.{w}\nAs The Honor Guard starts to climb up, he picks them off one by one.{w}\nIt was no problem. He'd just keep this up until all of them were dead.
column6: 他跳上桌面，占据了高度优势。{w}\n荣誉卫队开始攀爬，他便将它们逐个击破。{w}\n这不成问题。只要一直这样，直到把它们全部杀光。

column5: But they keep pouring into the room, and armor covers the table and floor.{w}\nThey're coming too fast — he can no longer fight them off one by one.{w}\nThey climb the table, and he suddenly fights three at the same time.
column6: 但它们不断涌入房间，桌上地上堆满了甲胄。{w}\n它们来得太快——他再也无法逐个应付。{w}\n它们爬上桌子，他骤然间要同时面对三个。

column5: He starts to tire, his limbs growing weak from all the fighting.{w}\nBut still, he doesn't stop. He never gave up without winning.{w}\nDon't accept defeat until the very end. Every gambler's rule.
column6: 他开始疲惫，四肢因连番厮杀而发软。{w}\n但他仍未停下。没赢之前，他从不放弃。{w}\n不到最后一刻绝不认输。这是每个赌徒的准则。

column5: As agile as he was dextrous, fighting with daggers was second nature.{w}\nBut he'd need more than that, at this rate. He needed some range.{w}\nAs the suits fall, he grabs one of their longswords to use.
column6: 他身手灵巧又敏捷，用匕首作战如同本能。{w}\n但照这势头，这还不够。他需要些攻击距离。{w}\n趁空甲倒下，他抓起一把它们的长剑来用。

column5: Come on, give up already! It's over!
column6: 来吧，快认输吧！结束了！

column5: It seems that they too, followed the rule of never accepting defeat.{w}\nSwords clash, as Pro is soon accosted from every possible angle.{w}\nA blade grazes his shoulder, and blood drips down his clothing.
column6: 看来它们也奉行着那绝不认输的准则。{w}\n兵刃相交，普洛很快遭到四面八方的围攻。{w}\n一柄剑擦过他的肩膀，鲜血顺着衣物滴落。

column5: This just urges him to fight on even further.{w}\nHowever, the horde never seems to go down in numbers.{w}\nThey run into the dining hall faster than he can take them out.
column6: 这反而激励他更加奋力厮杀。{w}\n然而，敌潮的数量似乎从未减少。{w}\n它们冲进宴会厅的速度，比他斩杀得还快。

column5: Soon enough, there's absolutely nowhere to go.{w}\nBut even as hope starts to dissipate, Pro doesn't give up.{w}\nHe continues fighting, until the floor is a sea, full of pieces of armor.
column6: 很快，便再无一处可退。{w}\n但即便希望开始消散，普洛也没有放弃。{w}\n他继续战斗，直到地面化作一片满是碎甲的海洋。

column5: If I'm going down, then I'm taking all of you with me!\nLet's give those historians something to write about!
column6: 既然我要倒下，那我也要拉上你们所有人！\n让那些史官有东西可写吧！

column5: A sword is plunged through his shoulder, and he stumbles back, crying.{w}\nGritting his teeth, he pulls it out, and starts using two swords simultaneously.{w}\nAs if they were an extension of his body, he fights with immense grace.
column6: 一柄剑刺穿他的肩膀，他踉跄后退，痛呼出声。{w}\n他咬紧牙关，将剑拔出，开始双剑并用。{w}\n仿佛那是他身体的延伸，他战斗的姿态优雅至极。

column5: The wound is pouring blood, and he starts to get lightheaded.{w}\nShaking his head, he tries to snap himself back into cognition.{w}\nBut a moment later, a sword is violently thrust through his side.
column6: 伤口血流如注，他开始头晕目眩。{w}\n他摇摇头，试图让自己恢复清醒。{w}\n但片刻之后，一柄剑狠狠刺穿了他的侧腹。

column5: He lets out a loud battle cry, a sort of scream, and keeps fighting on.{w}\nBut as made evident by his weaker swings — his time was limited.
column6: 他发出一声响亮的战吼，近乎嘶喊，继续奋战。{w}\n但愈发无力的挥砍已昭示——他的时间不多了。

column5: Don't... accept... defeat...
column6: 不要……认……输……

column5: He fights, almost delirious from blood loss.{w}\nIn a last ditch effort to survive, he jumps off the table.{w}\nIf he could just fight his way to the exit — he'd survive...!
column6: 他仍在战斗，因失血而几近神志不清。{w}\n为了求生做最后一搏，他跳下桌子。{w}\n只要能杀出一条血路到出口——他就能活下来……！

column5: A fantasy brought on by his deluded state, no doubt.{w}\nIt wouldn't have worked before, and it wouldn't work now.{w}\nThe white suits of armor on the ground are crimson with his blood.
column6: 这无疑是痴妄状态催生的幻想。{w}\n从前行不通，现在也行不通。{w}\n地上那些白色甲胄，已被他的鲜血染成深红。

column5: Moments later, something surprising happens.{w}\nThe Honor Guard spreads out, almost like they're retreating.{w}\nHe falls to his knees, curious as to what's going on in their minds.
column6: 片刻之后，意想不到的事发生了。{w}\n荣誉卫队散开，几乎像是在撤退。{w}\n他跪倒在地，好奇它们脑中在想些什么。

column5: They sheathe their blades, as Pro kneels in a puddle of his own blood.{w}\nSo that's what it was. An admission of victory — and their opponent's death.{w}\nHe cries, and tries to repeat himself once more, as if its a sort of mantra.
column6: 普洛跪在自己的一滩血中，它们却收剑入鞘。{w}\n原来如此。那是对胜利的宣告——以及对手之死的确认。{w}\n他哭着，再次试着重复那句话，仿佛某种咒语。

column5: Don't... accept...
column6: 不要……认……

column5: He falls down on his side, crying and bleeding out on the floor.{w}\nDon't accept defeat. At least, not until the very end.{w}\nUnfortunately, for him — it seemed like this was it.
column6: 他侧身倒下，哭着，在地板上流尽鲜血。{w}\n不要认输。至少，不到最后一刻绝不认输。{w}\n遗憾的是，对他而言——这似乎就是终点了。

column5: [firstname]... I'm sorry...
column6: [firstname]……对不起……

column5: My luck... had to run out... sometime...
column6: 我的运气……总有……用尽的时候……

column5: In his final moments, he comforts himself with warm thoughts.{w}\nThoughts as warm as the pool of blood that now covered the floor.{w}\nHe passes on with a smile, finding happiness in the success of his task.
column6: 在最后的时刻，他用温暖的思绪安慰自己。{w}\n那思绪和此刻覆盖地面的血泊一样温热。{w}\n他带着微笑离世，为自己的任务得以完成而感到幸福。

column5: Howl is completely surrounded, fighting to the best of his efforts.{w}\nA one-on-one fight would be no problem, but this was too much.{w}\nIn total, there must be tens of thousands of Honor Guard here.
column6: 豪尔被彻底包围，竭尽全力地战斗。{w}\n一对一的话毫无问题，但这样的数量实在太多。{w}\n这里总共恐怕有上万名荣誉卫队。

column5: Fighting with his fists, he punches the suits of armor into pieces.{w}\nHe preferred to use his own body as a weapon, rather than anything else.{w}\nOther people fought with extensions of their body, but he needed none of that.
column6: 他赤手空拳地战斗，把空甲一拳拳砸成碎片。{w}\n比起其他任何东西，他更愿意把自己的身体当作武器。{w}\n别人靠身体的延伸物作战，他则全不需要。

column5: One thing was for sure — he couldn't keep this up forever.{w}\nWith the power The Monarch absorbed, he was mortal, and vulnerable.{w}\nHowever, he used the sense of dread in order to fight with more determination.
column6: 有一点可以肯定——他不可能永远这样撑下去。{w}\n君主吸收了那股力量后，他已是凡人，会受伤、会死。{w}\n然而，他正是用这份恐惧感，让自己打得更决绝。

column5: In this moment, Howl was thankful that all of his power remained intact.{w}\nHad The Monarch heeded his request, he would surely be close to death.{w}\nThankful for that fact, he fought on with an ever increasing sense of determination.
column6: 此刻，豪尔庆幸自己的力量完好无损。{w}\n倘若君主当时应了他的请求，他必定早已濒死。{w}\n正因为心怀感激，他战斗的决心愈发坚定。

column5: Damek was nowhere to be seen, but Howl hoped that he was still alive.{w}\nThere were so many suits of armor, that it was impossible to keep track.{w}\nOne stray arrow, one thrown dagger, or one sneak attack — and it was over.
column6: 达梅克不见踪影，但豪尔希望他还活着。{w}\n空甲太多，根本无法一一留意。{w}\n一支流矢、一把掷来的匕首，或一次偷袭——就完了。

column5: As he punched through the suits of armor, he finally saw an ally.{w}\nChanging the direction of his assault, he fought his way toward them.{w}\nGreeting him with a smile, it was a relief to see a friendly face once again.
column6: 在击穿空甲之际，他终于看见一位战友。{w}\n他改变进攻方向，朝那人一路杀去。{w}\n对方笑着迎接他，再次见到熟悉的面孔，让他如释重负。

column5: Howl — watch out!
column6: 豪尔——小心！

column5: Vivien jumps behind Howl, taking out a suit that was sneaking up on him.{w}\nThanking his ally, Howl responded by doing the same — but behind Vivien.{w}\nNo matter where they stood, there was always an enemy in pursuit.
column6: 薇薇安跳到豪尔身后，解决掉一架正偷袭他的空甲。{w}\n豪尔向战友道谢，也以同样的方式回应——守住了薇薇安的后背。{w}\n无论他们站在何处，总有敌人穷追不舍。

column5: Arrows fly overhead every few seconds. The enemy archers were skilled.{w}\nHowl couldn't see, but he knew that those arrows hit home on his allies.{w}\nWith his back pressed against Vivien, their rears are finally protected.
column6: 每隔几秒就有箭矢从头顶飞过。敌方的弓箭手技艺精湛。{w}\n豪尔看不见，但他知道那些箭正射中他的战友。{w}\n他和薇薇安背靠着背，后背终于有了掩护。

column5: Vivien — status report.\nHow are you men doing?
column6: 薇薇安——汇报情况。\n你手下的人怎么样了？

column5: Not good, last time I checked.\nThere's just too many of them, Howl.\nAll we can do is wait for that bell to ring.
column6: 上次查看时不太妙。\n它们实在太多了，豪尔。\n我们能做的只有等那口钟敲响。

column5: And if it doesn't...?
column6: 要是它不响呢……？

column5: Vivien lunges forward, taking out several suits of armor.{w}\nThen, a moment later, he presses his back against Howl again.
column6: 薇薇安向前猛冲，解决掉几架空甲。{w}\n片刻之后，他再次把后背贴上豪尔。

column5: Then this is it for us.
column6: 那我们就到此为止了。

column5: The despair in his voice was clear.{w}\nThey could keep fighting, but things were looking bad.{w}\nEven if each man killed a hundred suits, they'd still be outnumbered.
column6: 他声音里的绝望清晰可闻。{w}\n他们可以继续战斗，但形势不妙。{w}\n就算每人杀上一百架空甲，他们依旧寡不敌众。

column5: Howl shakes his head, freeing himself from the onslaught of ash.{w}\nThe library, still ablaze, rained remnants of The Monarchy upon them.{w}\nThe Honor Guard seemed unimpeded by this, but not The Rebellion.
column6: 豪尔摇摇头，甩去扑面而来的灰烬。{w}\n仍在燃烧的藏书阁，将王室的残骸如雨般洒落在他们身上。{w}\n荣誉卫队似乎毫不受阻，反抗军却不然。

column5: It was almost as if, when the suits fought together, they shared one mind.{w}\nThis caused them to be weak on their own, but formidable as a group.{w}\nHowever, it meant that the more they killed, the weaker their enemy became.
column6: 几乎可以说，那些空甲并肩作战时，共享着同一个意志。{w}\n这使它们单独时孱弱，成群时却极其可怖。{w}\n不过，这也意味着他们杀得越多，敌人就越虚弱。

column5: Vivien, do not give up so easily.\nYou are set to rule the strongest nation in the world.\nWe cannot have you return home with stories of lost hope.
column6: 薇薇安，别这么轻易放弃。\n你注定要统治世上最强的国度。\n我们不能让你带着绝望的故事回家。

column5: As they talk, they keep fighting. The enemy never lets up for a second.
column6: 他们一边交谈，一边继续战斗。敌人一秒钟也不肯松懈。

column5: Then we better find it again, and fast.
column6: 那我们最好快点把它找回来。

column5: Arrows fly through the air once more, and screams fill the air.{w}\nThey knew their forces were dying. The suits had no need to scream.{w}\nHowl wasn't even sure if they felt pain, or feared their own demise.
column6: 箭矢再度破空而过，惨叫声响彻四周。{w}\n他们知道自己的部下正在死去。那些空甲无需惨叫。{w}\n豪尔甚至不确定它们是否会感到疼痛，或恐惧自己的消亡。

column5: And he wondered if those things would be a weakness, or a strength.{w}\nHis knuckles become bloody, and cracked, as they fight for their lives.{w}\nThey continued to protect each other, fighting as if they were one body.
column6: 他思忖着，这些究竟是弱点，还是优势。{w}\n在他们拼死搏杀之际，他的指节渐渐染血、开裂。{w}\n他们继续互相掩护，如同同一个躯体般战斗。

column5: We need to change up our strategy.\nIf we don't, then they'll outsmart us.
column6: 我们得改变策略。\n不然的话，它们会比我们更胜一筹。

column5: Vivien didn't respond.
column6: 薇薇安没有回应。

column5: Vivien...?
column6: 薇薇安……？

column5: Vivien shakes his head, panting heavily.
column6: 薇薇安摇摇头，剧烈地喘着气。

column5: Sorry — it's just taking a lot out of me.\nI think I need to get back to the library.
column6: 抱歉——这实在太消耗我了。\n我想我得回藏书阁去了。

column5: Will you be okay on your own?
column6: 你一个人没问题吗？

column5: Yeah, I'll be fine. Will you?
column6: 嗯，我没事。你呢？

column5: Yeah. Go now, while you have an opening.\nWe will continue to fight them off.
column6: 没事。趁现在有空隙，快走吧。\n我们会继续挡住它们。

column5: Vivien nods, and then runs off toward the library.{w}\nSoon enough, he disappears into the crowd of suits.{w}\nHowl's back is vulnerable once more, but he still fights.
column6: 薇薇安点点头，朝藏书阁跑去。{w}\n很快，他便消失在空甲的浪潮中。{w}\n豪尔的后背再度暴露，但他依然战斗着。

column5: Vivien...?
column6: 薇薇安……？

column5: Howl turns around to look, and Vivien falls limp to the ground.{w}\nA small legion of arrows found their home in his body.{w}\nThere's nothing he can do. The shots were fatal.
column6: 豪尔转身去看，薇薇安却软软地倒在地上。{w}\n一小群箭矢扎进了他的身体。{w}\n他无能为力。那些箭是致命的。

column5: With unseen archers targeting his location, he needed to run.{w}\nHe's vulnerable from every angle, and he had no choice but to fight.{w}\nHe looks around frantically to find the archers, but it's no use.
column6: 看不见的弓箭手瞄准了他的位置，他必须跑起来。{w}\n他四面八方都暴露无遗，却只能继续战斗。{w}\n他狂乱地环顾，想找出那些弓箭手，却毫无用处。

column5: Howl — watch out...!
column6: 豪尔——小心……！

column5: Draycu jumps behind Howl, taking out a suit that was sneaking up on him.{w}\nThanking his ally, Howl responded by doing the same — but behind Draycu.{w}\nNo matter where they stood, there was always an enemy in pursuit of them.
column6: 德雷库跳到豪尔身后，解决掉一架正偷袭他的空甲。{w}\n豪尔向战友道谢，也以同样的方式回应——守住了德雷库的后背。{w}\n无论他们站在何处，总有敌人穷追不舍。

column5: Arrows fly overhead every few seconds. The enemy archers were skilled.{w}\nHowl couldn't see, but he knew that those arrows hit home on his allies.{w}\nWith his back pressed against Draycu, their rears are finally protected.
column6: 每隔几秒就有箭矢从头顶飞过。敌方的弓箭手技艺精湛。{w}\n豪尔看不见，但他知道那些箭正射中他的战友。{w}\n他和德雷库背靠着背，后背终于有了掩护。

column5: Status report, Draycu.\nHow are your men doing?
column6: 汇报情况，德雷库。\n你手下的人怎么样了？

column5: Not good, unfortunately.\nThere's just too many of those suits, Howl.\nAll we can really do is wait for that bell to ring.
column6: 很遗憾，不太妙。\n那些空甲实在太多了，豪尔。\n我们真正能做的，只有等那口钟敲响。

column5: And if it doesn't...?
column6: 要是它不响呢……？

column5: Draycu lunges forward, taking our several suits of armor.{w}\nThen, a moment later, he presses his back against Howl again.
column6: 德雷库向前猛冲，解决掉几架空甲。{w}\n片刻之后，他再次把后背贴上豪尔。

column5: Then we die with honor.\nWe fight to the bitter end.
column6: 那我们就光荣赴死。\n我们战斗到最后一刻。

column5: The despair in his voice was clear.{w}\nThey could keep fighting, but things were looking bad.{w}\nEven if each man killed a hundred suits, they'd still be outnumbered.
column6: 他声音里的绝望清晰可闻。{w}\n他们可以继续战斗，但形势不妙。{w}\n就算每人杀上一百架空甲，他们依旧寡不敌众。

column5: Howl shakes his head, freeing himself from the onslaught of ash.{w}\nThe library, still ablaze, rained remnants of The Monarchy upon them.{w}\nThe Honor Guard seemed unimpeded by this, but not The Rebellion.
column6: 豪尔摇摇头，甩去扑面而来的灰烬。{w}\n仍在燃烧的藏书阁，将王室的残骸如雨般洒落在他们身上。{w}\n荣誉卫队似乎毫不受阻，反抗军却不然。

column5: It was almost as if, when the suits fought together, they shared one mind.{w}\nThis caused them to be weak on their own, but formidable as a group.{w}\nHowever, it meant that the more they killed, the weaker their enemy became.
column6: 几乎可以说，那些空甲并肩作战时，共享着同一个意志。{w}\n这使它们单独时孱弱，成群时却极其可怖。{w}\n不过，这也意味着他们杀得越多，敌人就越虚弱。

column5: Do not give up so easily, Draycu.\nYou rule Alarinthia, the strongest nation in the world.\nYou cannot afford to return home with stories of lost hope.
column6: 别这么轻易放弃，德雷库。\n你统治着阿拉林西亚，世上最强的国度。\n你绝不能带着绝望的故事回家。

column5: As they talk, they keep fighting. The enemy doesn't let up for a second.
column6: 他们一边交谈，一边继续战斗。敌人一刻也不肯松懈。

column5: Then let's find it again, and fast.
column6: 那我们就快点把它找回来。

column5: Arrows fly through the air once more, and screams fill the air.{w}\nThey knew their forces were dying. The suits had no need to scream.{w}\nHowl wasn't even sure if they felt pain, or feared their own demise.
column6: 箭矢再度破空而过，惨叫声响彻四周。{w}\n他们知道自己的部下正在死去。那些空甲无需惨叫。{w}\n豪尔甚至不确定它们是否会感到疼痛，或恐惧自己的消亡。

column5: And he wondered if those things would be a weakness, or a strength.{w}\nHis knuckles become bloody, and cracked, as they fight for their lives.{w}\nThey continued to protect each other, fighting as if they were one body.
column6: 他思忖着，这些究竟是弱点，还是优势。{w}\n在他们拼死搏杀之际，他的指节渐渐染血、开裂。{w}\n他们继续互相掩护，如同同一个躯体般战斗。

column5: We cannot stay like this forever.\nThey'll find a way to outsmart us.
column6: 我们不能一直这样下去。\n它们会找到法子胜过我们。

column5: Draycu didn't respond.
column6: 德雷库没有回应。

column5: Draycu...?
column6: 德雷库……？

column5: Draycu shakes his head, and pants heavily.
column6: 德雷库摇摇头，剧烈地喘着气。

column5: Sorry — just needed a breather.\nI haven't had a fight like this in ages.
column6: 抱歉——只是需要喘口气。\n我好多年没打过这样的仗了。

column5: Howl nods, agreeing with his ally.
column6: 豪尔点点头，认同战友的话。

column5: I'm afraid that we must part ways, though.\nThe same strategy is only effective for so long.
column6: 不过，恐怕我们得分头行动了。\n同一套策略的有效时间终究有限。

column5: Yes, of course.\nThat same tactic won me many coliseum battles.\nGood luck, Howl — and take a few out for me.
column6: 是啊，当然。\n同样的战术曾让我赢下许多场竞技场之战。\n祝你好运，豪尔——替我多干掉几个。

column5: With a smile, Draycu runs, and disappears into a crowd of suits.{w}\nHowl wouldn't have had time to say goodbye, even if he wanted to.{w}\nHe stands there, alone once more, with nothing else to do but fight.
column6: 德雷库笑着跑去，消失在空甲的浪潮中。{w}\n就算豪尔想道别，也没时间了。{w}\n他站在原地，再度孤身一人，除了战斗别无他事可做。

column5: Draycu...?
column6: 德雷库……？

column5: Howl turns around to look, and Draycu falls limp to the ground.{w}\nA small legion of arrows found their home in his body.{w}\nThere's nothing he can do. The shots were fatal.
column6: 豪尔转身去看，德雷库却软软地倒在地上。{w}\n一小群箭矢扎进了他的身体。{w}\n他无能为力。那些箭是致命的。

column5: With unseen archers targeting his location, he needed to run.{w}\nHe's vulnerable from every angle, and he had no choice but to fight.{w}\nHe looks around frantically to find the archers, but it's no use.
column6: 看不见的弓箭手瞄准了他的位置，他必须跑起来。{w}\n他四面八方都暴露无遗，却只能继续战斗。{w}\n他狂乱地环顾，想找出那些弓箭手，却毫无用处。

column5: All he can do is face the enemy, and his fate, head on.{w}\nCharging into the crowd with a scream, rage wells up within him.{w}\nThere are no allies to be seen. Just target after target waiting to be killed.
column6: 他所能做的，只有直面敌人与自己的命运。{w}\n他嘶吼着冲入人群，怒火在胸中翻涌。{w}\n再也看不到任何战友。只有一个个等着被杀的靶子。

column5: And that's what happens next. He shatters the enemies like weak glass.{w}\nThey fall to the ground, leaving a trail of carnage in his wake.{w}\nHe had killed more than his fair share, and still went on.
column6: 接下来便是如此。他像击碎脆弱玻璃般粉碎敌人。{w}\n它们倒在地上，在他身后留下一路残骸。{w}\n他早已杀得远超本分，却仍在继续。

column5: Eventually, a barrage of arrows assaults him.{w}\nPiercing through his torso, it causes him to grunt in immense pain.{w}\nHe does his best to shake it off, but it's almost too much to bear.
column6: 最终，一阵箭雨向他袭来。{w}\n箭矢穿透他的躯干，剧痛令他闷哼出声。{w}\n他竭力想撑住，却几乎无法承受。

column5: Now that the excess spirits were removed from his body, he was mortal.{w}\nBecause of that, he lets the arrows stay inside of his body.{w}\nPulling them out would be nothing short of a death sentence.
column6: 既然体内多余的灵体已被剥离，他便成了凡人。{w}\n正因如此，他任由箭矢留在体内。{w}\n把它们拔出，无异于宣判死刑。

column5: But so too, was rushing headfirst into a horde of those suits.{w}\nAll of a sudden, it's harder for him to keep track of everything happening.{w}\nConfusion sets in, and he starts longing for his ally to return and help him.
column6: 可一头扎进那群空甲之中，同样也是死路。{w}\n突然间，他越来越难以掌握周遭的一切。{w}\n困惑袭来，他开始盼着战友回来帮他。

column5: But even if they did come back, they would arrive a moment too late.{w}\nHe turns around, looking for more enemies — and one is {i}right{/i} there.{w}\nThey thrust their longsword deep in his gut, and he stumbles back.
column6: 但就算他们真回来了，也只会慢上一步。{w}\n他转身寻找更多敌人——而那一个{i}就{/i}在眼前。{w}\n那架空甲把长剑深深刺进他的腹部，他踉跄后退。

column5: But then he quickly lunges forward, destroying the suit with a harsh punch.{w}\nMore suits crumble down around him, and miraculously, he's still fighting.{w}\nIt was miraculous that he was still standing. He fought on with fervor.
column6: 但他随即猛冲上前，一记重拳将那架空甲击碎。{w}\n更多空甲在他周围崩落，而他奇迹般地仍在战斗。{w}\n他还能站着，本身便是奇迹。他带着狂热继续厮杀。

column5: However, the archers from before were preparing another shot.{w}\nMoments later, his back is full of arrows, as they hit their target.{w}\nHis body starts to feel numb, and he falls to his knees with a cry.
column6: 然而，先前的弓箭手正在准备又一轮射击。{w}\n片刻之后，箭矢命中目标，他的后背插满了箭。{w}\n他的身体开始发麻，惨叫着跪倒在地。

column5: The Honor Guard surrounds him, and he's too weak to fight back.{w}\nIn his current state, all he could do was stand his ground and seek mercy.{w}\nYet he chooses not to. He'd never accept defeat without putting up a fight.
column6: 荣誉卫队将他团团围住，他已虚弱得无力反抗。{w}\n以他现在的状态，所能做的只有驻足原地、乞求怜悯。{w}\n但他偏不。不战而降，他绝不接受。

column5: He takes out a few more suits before they start to fight back.{w}\nPerhaps they were giving him a chance to surrender, and accept death.{w}\nHowever, such opportunity has passed, and swords soon assault him.
column6: 在它们开始反击前，他又干掉了好几架空甲。{w}\n或许它们是在给他机会投降，接受死亡。{w}\n然而，这机会已然错过，刀剑很快向他袭来。

column5: They work quick, covering Howl's entire body with wounds.{w}\nHe falls down on the ground, trembling from the intense pain.{w}\nBlood pools around him, spilling until there's nothing left to spill.
column6: 它们动作麻利，在豪尔全身留下累累伤口。{w}\n他倒在地上，因剧痛而浑身颤抖。{w}\n鲜血在他周围积成水洼，一直流到再无可流。

column5: Then, The Honor Guard walks away, realizing they had won.{w}\nHowl lays there, looking up at the sky, and the steadily falling ash.{w}\nIt covers him, and he becomes one with the remnants of his people.
column6: 随后，荣誉卫队意识到自己已经获胜，转身离去。{w}\n豪尔躺在那里，仰望着天空与不断飘落的灰烬。{w}\n灰烬覆盖了他，他与族人的残骸融为一体。

column5: Eventually a barrage of arrows assaults him.{w}\nPiercing through his torso, he grunts in immense pain.{w}\nHowever, the pain was minimal compared to the pain he normally felt.
column6: 最终，一阵箭雨向他袭来。{w}\n箭矢穿透他的躯干，剧痛令他闷哼出声。{w}\n然而，与他惯常承受的痛楚相比，这根本微不足道。

column5: He pulls out the arrows, and throws them down on the ground.{w}\nBlood spills from the wounds, but he shows no signs of pain.{w}\nSuch wounds would do nothing to a body powered by The Monarchy.
column6: 他拔出箭矢，扔在地上。{w}\n鲜血从伤口涌出，他却毫无痛楚之色。{w}\n这样的伤，对一具由王室之力驱动的躯体毫无作用。

column5: All he had to do was fight until the bell was rung.{w}\nBut that was the question on everybody's minds right now.{w}\nWith such an immense task before him, would Fortaime succeed?
column6: 他所要做的，只是战斗到钟声敲响。{w}\n但这正是此刻所有人心中悬着的问题。{w}\n面对如此艰巨的任务，福泰姆能成功吗？

column5: It seemed — that right now — almost everything lay in his hands.{w}\nHowl fought ruthlessly, hoping to hear the bell, and find relief.{w}\nBut with each passing second, the hope within him dwindled.
column6: 现在看来——此刻——几乎一切都系于他一人之手。{w}\n豪尔无情地厮杀，盼着听见钟声，得到解脱。{w}\n但每过一秒，他心中的希望便黯淡一分。

column5: Fortaime pants heavily, panicking with an arrow in his side.{w}\nHe knew that if he pulled it out, things would only get worse.{w}\nIt would be best to keep it inside, until he could find some help.
column6: 福泰姆剧烈喘息，侧腹中箭令他惊慌失措。{w}\n他知道一旦拔出，情况只会更糟。{w}\n最好先让它留在体内，直到找到人帮忙。

column5: It wouldn't be fatal, so that gave him great relief on its own.{w}\nHiding in a spare room he found, he needed to take a breather.{w}\nIt was perfect timing, as suits started to scurry around outside.
column6: 这伤不致命，单是这点就让他大大松了口气。{w}\n他躲进一间找到的空房，需要喘口气。{w}\n时机正好，外面的空甲开始四处乱窜。

column5: It can't be too far away.\nHow high up does this castle even go...?
column6: 应该不会太远了。\n这座城堡到底有多高……？

column5: He shakes his head, realizing there was only one way to find out.{w}\nBut as he goes to sneak out of the room, he bumps into a table.{w}\nA bottle of wine falls off the side, and shatters with an echo.
column6: 他摇摇头，意识到只有一个办法能知道答案。{w}\n但当他正要溜出房间时，撞到了一张桌子。{w}\n一瓶葡萄酒从边上掉落，碎裂声回荡开来。

column5: His entire body tenses up as he hears The Honor Guard stop moving.{w}\nHe runs to the other side of the room, and hides behind a curtain.{w}\nIt would've been easy to sneak around them, if not for the wine.
column6: 听到荣誉卫队停下脚步，他全身都绷紧了。{w}\n他跑到房间另一头，躲到窗帘后。{w}\n若不是那瓶酒，绕过它们本会很容易。

column5: Now, every single suit of armor in that hallway would know he's here.{w}\nHe remains as still as possible as one of them enters the room to scout.{w}\nThe suit kneels down to inspect the broken glass. Then looks over to the curtain.
column6: 现在，那条走廊里每一架空甲都会知道他在此处。{w}\n其中一架进屋搜查时，他尽可能一动不动。{w}\n那架空甲蹲下查看碎玻璃，随后朝窗帘望来。

column5: His cover was blown. He made a small trail of wine with his footsteps.{w}\nHe holds his breath as the suit of armor makes its way to his location.{w}\nThen, a few moments later, it plunges its sword right in the curtain.
column6: 他的掩护暴露了。他的脚印拖出一道小小的酒渍。{w}\n那架空甲朝他所在的位置走来，他屏住呼吸。{w}\n片刻之后，它把剑径直刺进窗帘。

column5: Fortaime dodges to the left, then rips the curtain down from the wall.{w}\nWrapping it around the suit of armor, he has it in a strong chokehold.{w}\nHe hesitates for a few moments, and then snaps his enemy's neck.
column6: 福泰姆向左闪避，随即把窗帘从墙上扯下。{w}\n他用窗帘缠住那架空甲，牢牢勒住它的脖颈。{w}\n他犹豫了片刻，然后拧断了敌人的脖子。

column5: The suit crumbles, but has nowhere to fall, being held together by the curtain.{w}\nHe slowly rests it on the ground. This was his first real fight. His first kill.{w}\nIf he survived to ring that bell, he knew he would never be the same.
column6: 空甲崩解，却被窗帘兜住，无处坠落。{w}\n他缓缓将它放到地上。这是他第一场真正的战斗。他第一次杀人。{w}\n如果他能活下来敲响那口钟，他知道自己将再也不是从前的自己。

column5: He slowly unravels the curtain, and grabs the sword belonging to the suit.{w}\nAs soon as he does, more of them enter the room, to check up on their ally.{w}\nFortaime wondered if they felt emotion. If they'd mourn the suit he killed.
column6: 他慢慢解开窗帘，抓起那架空甲的长剑。{w}\n他刚拿到手，更多空甲便进屋查看同伴。{w}\n福泰姆想知道它们是否有情感。是否会为他杀掉的这架空甲哀悼。

column5: They drew their swords, but Fortaime wasn't sure what prompted it.{w}\nAnger at their dead ally — or perhaps blind loyalty to The Triumvirate.{w}\nHe'd never know, and in that moment, he realized it was for the best.
column6: 它们拔出了剑，但福泰姆不确定是何缘故。{w}\n是为死去的同伴愤怒——还是出于对三人执政团的盲目忠诚。{w}\n他永远不会知道，而在那一刻，他意识到这样也好。

column5: Sword clashed against sword, as he fought for his life.{w}\nBut not just his. Almost everybody else's lives were at stake, too.{w}\nThey were relying on him to ring that bell; and he couldn't let them down!
column6: 刀剑相交，他为自己的性命而战。{w}\n但不只是他自己的。几乎所有人的性命都悬于一线。{w}\n他们都指望他去敲响那口钟；他不能让他们失望！

column5: All he had to do was survive...
column6: 他所要做的，只是活下来……

column5: When we get inside the castle, I notice that it's completely empty.{w}\nPro must've been successful. Otherwise, this place would be full.{w}\nI'm thankful, but unable to find happiness. Not after losing Valessa.
column6: 我们进入城堡时，我发现里面空无一人。{w}\n普洛一定成功了。否则，这里本该挤满了人。{w}\n我很感激，却无法感到快乐。失去瓦莱莎之后，我做不到。

column5: Sure, I didn't see her final moments, but she was dead.{w}\nThere's no way somebody could survive an attack like that.{w}\nMy friend. One of my first friends. I'm in complete disbelief.
column6: 的确，我没看到她最后的时刻，但她死了。{w}\n没人能在那样的攻击下活下来。{w}\n我的朋友。我最早的朋友之一。我完全无法相信。

column5: Hey, snap out of it. We need you in good shape.\nI know what you saw out there, but she could still be alive.\nIf we just stand here moping, then we might as well surrender.
column6: 嘿，振作起来。我们需要你保持良好状态。\n我知道你在外面看到了什么，但她也许还活着。\n要是我们杵在这儿自怨自艾，那还不如直接投降。

column5: I shake my head. He was wrong, and I knew it.{w}\nValessa was dead, and I had to learn to accept that.{w}\nI start walking toward the stairs, wanting nothing but revenge.
column6: 我摇摇头。他错了，我清楚这一点。{w}\n瓦莱莎已经死了，我必须学会接受。{w}\n我朝楼梯走去，心中只有复仇。

column5: When we get inside the castle, I notice that it's completely empty.{w}\nI'm filled with hope. Pro must've been successful with his distraction.{w}\nOtherwise, this place would be teeming with those suits of armor.
column6: 我们进入城堡时，我发现里面空无一人。{w}\n我心中充满希望。普洛的牵制一定成功了。{w}\n否则，这里本该挤满了那些空甲。

column5: All we had to do was make our way to the top, and take them down.{w}\nWith The Triumvirate dead, and that bell rung — victory was ours.{w}\nI cross my fingers, hoping that Fortaime's travels are going well.
column6: 我们所要做的，就是一路登上顶层，将他们拿下。{w}\n只要三人执政团一死，钟声一响——胜利便属于我们。{w}\n我暗自祈祷，希望福泰姆的行程一切顺利。

column5: Wow, I haven't been to this place in ages.\nIt doesn't look any different, though. Just as uninviting.\nWe want to go right up those stairs, [firstname]. This is it.
column6: 哇，我好多年没来过这地方了。\n不过看起来毫无变化。依旧让人望而生畏。\n我们要直接上那些楼梯，[firstname]。就是现在。

column5: I nod. He was right — this was the end of our journey.{w}\nAfter everything I've been through, I was finally in their castle.{w}\nI start walking toward the stairs. My next actions were clear.
column6: 我点点头。他说得对——这是我们旅途的终点。{w}\n历经千辛万苦，我终于来到了他们的城堡。{w}\n我朝楼梯走去。接下来的行动已然清晰。

column5: Hey, not so fast. You should let {i}me{/i} take point.\nI know the layout of this castle, and where to go.\nIt gets a bit confusing up there. Trust me on that.
column6: 嘿，别急。该让{i}我{/i}来打头阵。\n我熟悉这座城堡的布局，也知道该往哪走。\n上面有点容易迷路。这点你信我。

column5: Confusing...? How so?
column6: 容易迷路……？怎么说？

column5: Lots of stairs. I hope you're okay with that.\nAnd be careful, we don't want to fall into a trap.\nThis place is massive. It would be easy to ambush us.
column6: 楼梯多得很。希望你受得了。\n还有，小心点，我们可不想中埋伏。\n这地方巨大无比。很容易被伏击。

column5: Let's just say there's lots of stairs coming up.\nAnd be careful, alright? We don't want to fall into a trap.\nWe're in their territory now. An ambush would be child's play.
column6: 这么说吧，接下来有一大堆楼梯。\n小心点，好吗？我们可不想中埋伏。\n我们现在在他们的地盘上。设伏对他们来说易如反掌。

column5: Not a second later, somebody enters the room from the opposite side.{w}\nIt's that man from our HQ. The one with Sovy, clad in white and gold.{w}\nHe descends the stairs, laughing at us. A horde of suits follows.
column6: 不出片刻，有人从对面走进了房间。{w}\n是我们总部见过的那个人。和索维在一起、身披白金装束的那个。{w}\n他走下楼梯，冲着我们大笑。一群空甲紧随其后。

column5: Ambush...? No, I don't play cheap. Not like Sovy.\nI'd merely like to call this a \"welcoming party\" of sorts.\nAn ambush is unexpected. Surely, you {i}knew{/i} I'd be here.
column6: 埋伏……？不，我不玩这种下三滥。我可不像索维。\n我更愿意把这场面叫做某种“欢迎会”。\n埋伏是出其不意的。你们{i}早该知道{/i}我会在这儿。

column5: I unsheathe my blade, and hold it out toward our enemy.{w}\nThere was no time to argue semantics with the likes of him.{w}\nBut, as if to guard me, Ulric and Sovy step forward, getting in the way.
column6: 我拔出刀刃，指向我们的敌人。{w}\n没时间跟他这种人抠字眼。{w}\n但乌尔里克和索维像是要护住我，上前挡在了中间。

column5: Halin, don't you think it's time you gave up...?\nYou've been bound to their will, following orders for so long.\nLet us remove that curse. We can give you your freedom back!
column6: 哈林，你不觉得是时候放弃了吗……？\n你被他们的意志束缚，听命行事太久了。\n让我们解除那道诅咒。我们能还你自由！

column5: Clearly an act. Sovy wanted Halin dead.{w}\nThat, and he could never agree. He was under their thrall.{w}\nA moment later, Halin disappears into the crowd of suits.
column6: 显然是在做戏。索维想要哈林的命。{w}\n况且，哈林绝不可能答应。他被他们的意志所控制。{w}\n片刻之后，哈林消失在空甲的浪潮中。

column5: Freedom...? I don't need freedom.\nI exist to serve The Triumvirate, and that is final.\nYou did too — but you threw it away in your folly.
column6: 自由……？我不需要自由。\n我存在的意义就是效忠三人执政团，这一点无可更改。\n你曾经也是——可你愚蠢地把它抛弃了。

column5: I unsheathe my blade, and hold it out toward our enemy.{w}\nThere was no time to argue semantics with the likes of him.{w}\nBut, as if to guard me, Ulric steps forward, getting in the way.
column6: 我拔出刀刃，指向我们的敌人。{w}\n没时间跟他这种人抠字眼。{w}\n但乌尔里克像是要护住我，上前挡在了中间。

column5: Look — we don't need to fight you.\nI know what you are. A slave to The Triumvirate.\nWe can fix that, Halin. We can remove the curse.
column6: 听着——我们不必与你为敌。\n我知道你是什么。三人执政团的奴隶。\n我们能改变这一点，哈林。我们能解除那道诅咒。

column5: It would never work. Halin was under their thrall.{w}\nEven considering this offer would be an act of defiance.{w}\nInstead of responding, Halin disappears into the crowd of suits.
column6: 这永远不会奏效。哈林被他们的意志所控制。{w}\n哪怕考虑这个提议，都算是一种违抗。{w}\n哈林没有回应，而是消失在空甲的浪潮中。

column5: Curse...? You call this a curse?\nI embody The Triumvirate's will, and command their army.\nYou are the cursed ones. You fight for the dream of a fool.
column6: 诅咒……？你把这叫做诅咒？\n我是三人执政团意志的化身，统率他们的军队。\n你们才是被诅咒的人。你们为一个蠢货的梦想而战。

column5: The suits of armor reach the bottom of the stairs.{w}\nBut Halin is nowhere to be seen. We just hear his voice.{w}\nHe must've used the confusion of the crowd to escape.
column6: 空甲抵达楼梯底部。{w}\n但哈林已不见踪影。我们只听见他的声音。{w}\n他一定是借着人群的混乱逃走了。

column5: You stand in the realm of Gods, now.\nIt is time that you spoke with your resolve.\nIf it is strong enough, then you will find me.
column6: 你们此刻站在神明的领域。\n是时候用你们的决心来说话了。\n若它足够坚定，你们便能找到我。

column5: The Honor Guard draws their swords, as Halin's laughter fills the room.
column6: 哈林的笑声响彻房间，荣誉卫队拔出了剑。

column5: And if it is not — then you will perish.\nSo do it. Show me the determination of your Rebellion.\nSpeak against your Gods, and see how they answer!
column6: 若是不够——你们便会灭亡。\n那就来吧。让我看看你们反抗军的决心。\n开口反抗你们的神明，看看它们如何回应！

column5: At Halin's command, The Honor Guard charges in our direction.{w}\nSovy and Ulric are the first to fight, making sure that I'm protected.{w}\nBut I make sure to play my part. I take them down with similar ease.
column6: 随着哈林一声令下，荣誉卫队朝我们冲来。{w}\n索维和乌尔里克率先迎战，确保我受到保护。{w}\n但我也尽好自己的本分，同样轻松地将它们击倒。

column5: The suits of armor stand no chance against The Blade of Exodus.{w}\nThe same could be said of Ulric's greatsword, and Sovy's fists.{w}\nI'm confident in our victory, but I try not to get too cocky.
column6: 空甲在流亡之刃面前毫无胜算。{w}\n乌尔里克的巨剑与索维的双拳也是如此。{w}\n我对胜利充满信心，但尽量不让自己太过自负。

column5: It seemed like there were almost a thousand suits of armor here.{w}\nThough we were doing good now, our bodies could easily weaken.{w}\nA viable tactic. Wear out your enemy with excessive numbers.
column6: 这里似乎有将近一千架空甲。{w}\n虽然我们眼下占优，但体力很容易耗尽。{w}\n这是个可行的战术。用压倒性的数量拖垮敌人。

column5: As we fight, we find ourselves surrounded more and more.{w}\nThe Honor Guard seems to have almost \"herded\" us to a specific location.{w}\nI stand back to back with Sovy and Ulric, and we're all panting heavily.
column6: 战斗之中，我们发现自己被越围越紧。{w}\n荣誉卫队似乎几乎把我们“驱赶”到了某个特定位置。{w}\n我和索维、乌尔里克背靠着背，全都剧烈喘息。

column5: Ulric, put away your sword.
column6: 乌尔里克，把剑收起来。

column5: Huh...?
Don't you remember...?
column6: 你不记得了吗……？

column5: They both look at me.
column6: 他们两人都看向我。

column5: Yeah, of course.
column6: 嗯，当然。

column5: He sheathes his massive blade as the suits close in on us.
column6: 空甲向我们逼近，他收起那把巨刃。

column5: [firstname], open your mind to us.\nTreat us as extensions of your body.
column6: [firstname]，向我们敞开心灵。\n把我们当作你身体的延伸。

column5: I'm confused, but I nod.{w}\nWe need to take action — and now.{w}\nI lunge forward, and destroy one of the suits.
column6: 我虽困惑，还是点了点头。{w}\n我们必须行动——立刻。{w}\n我向前猛冲，摧毁了一架空甲。

column5: Good. Now it's my turn.
column6: 很好。现在轮到我了。

column5: Then, the blade moves from my hands, to Sovy's.{w}\nHe does the same as me, and destroys several suits.{w}\nAs if passing a baton, Ulric is up next, swinging the blade.
column6: 随后，刀刃从我的手中移到了索维手中。{w}\n他如我一般，摧毁了好几架空甲。{w}\n如同传递接力棒，接下来轮到乌尔里克挥动刀刃。

column5: It's been too long, Sovy.
column6: 太久没这样了，索维。

column5: Then, almost instantaneously, it's back in my hands. I keep fighting.{w}\nWe're pressed back to back, exchanging the blade with our power.{w}\nPhasing it from person to person as needed, we're almost one mind.
column6: 紧接着，几乎在一瞬间，它又回到我手中。我继续战斗。{w}\n我们背贴着背，用力量传递着刀刃。{w}\n按需在彼此之间相位转移，我们几乎心意相通。

column5: Yes. Really gets my blood boiling.
column6: 是啊。真让我热血沸腾。

column5: As if it's an intricately choreographed dance, we continue to fight.{w}\nIn this moment, we really did command the blade. We were its owners.{w}\nI feel unstoppable. But then I realize, could The Triumvirate do this as well...?
column6: 我们继续战斗，仿佛一支编排精妙的舞蹈。{w}\n这一刻，我们真正掌控了刀刃。我们是它的主人。{w}\n我感到势不可挡。但随即我意识到，三人执政团是否也能做到……？

column5: If they could, then we're in for a difficult fight.
column6: 如果他们也能，那这场仗就难打了。

column5: Over here...!
column6: 这边……！

column5: I let Ulric take the blade, and we continue passing it around.{w}\nIt isn't much longer until the horde is thinned out. We're winning...!{w}\nThis is true teamwork. Unlike anything I've seen in my entire life.
column6: 我让乌尔里克接过刀刃，我们继续轮流传递。{w}\n没过多久，敌潮便被削减殆尽。我们要赢了……！{w}\n这才是真正的团队协作。是我一生中从未见过的。

column5: [firstname], look out!
column6: [firstname]，小心！

column5: I take back the blade, and destroy the suits in front of me.{w}\nTheir numbers have easily halved in just a few short minutes.{w}\nAt this rate, we'd be free to take those stairs at any second.
column6: 我收回刀刃，摧毁面前的空甲。{w}\n短短几分钟内，它们的数量就轻松减半。{w}\n照这速度，我们随时都能腾出身来登上那些楼梯。

column5: They mean to kill us with mindless slaves.\nI wish they had the courage to meet us face to face.
column6: 他们想用没有心智的奴隶来杀死我们。\n我倒希望他们有胆量与我们正面相见。

column5: The Triumvirate must've been scared. I could feel it.{w}\nIn the end, all tyrants have left to do is cower in fright.{w}\nWhatever game they were playing, it would soon be over.
column6: 三人执政团一定是怕了。我能感觉到。{w}\n到头来，暴君们只剩下瑟瑟发抖的份。{w}\n无论他们在玩什么把戏，很快就要结束了。

column5: We continue our dance, until the last suit of armor has fallen.{w}\nThough we're reduced to exhausted messes — we had won.{w}\nTaking deep breaths, we try and regain our composure.
column6: 我们的共舞持续到最后一架空甲倒下。{w}\n尽管我们已累得不成样子——但我们赢了。{w}\n我们深吸着气，努力平复心神。

column5: So — up we go?
column6: 那么——我们上去吗？

column5: Yeah.
column6: 嗯。

column5: I phase the blade back into my hands, and sheathe it.{w}\nLooking toward the stairs, it seems our next goal is clear.{w}\nWhen we got up there, we'd make him regret taunting us.
column6: 我将刀刃相位转移回手中，收入鞘内。{w}\n望向楼梯，我们接下来的目标已然明确。{w}\n等我们上去，就让他为嘲弄我们而后悔。

column5: At Halin's command, The Honor Guard charges in our direction.{w}\nUlric is the first to fight, using that massive greatsword to protect me.{w}\nBut I make sure to play my part. I take them down with similar ease.
column6: 随着哈林一声令下，荣誉卫队朝我们冲来。{w}\n乌尔里克率先迎战，用那把巨剑护住我。{w}\n但我也尽好自己的本分，同样轻松地将它们击倒。

column5: The suits of armor stood no chance against The Blade of Exodus.{w}\nBut in this case — they also stood no chance against Ulric.{w}\nI'm confident in our victory, but I try not to get cocky.
column6: 空甲在流亡之刃面前毫无胜算。{w}\n但这一次——它们在乌尔里克面前同样毫无胜算。{w}\n我对胜利充满信心，但尽量不让自己太过自负。

column5: It seemed like there were almost a thousand suits of armor here.{w}\nThough we were doing good now, our bodies could easily weaken.{w}\nA viable tactic. Wear out your enemy with excessive numbers.
column6: 这里似乎有将近一千架空甲。{w}\n虽然我们眼下占优，但体力很容易耗尽。{w}\n这是个可行的战术。用压倒性的数量拖垮敌人。

column5: As we fight, we find ourselves surrounded more and more.{w}\nThe Honor Guard seems to have \"herded\" us into a specific location.{w}\nStanding back to back with Ulric, we pant heavily, a panic rising within us.
column6: 战斗之中，我们发现自己被越围越紧。{w}\n荣誉卫队似乎把我们“驱赶”到了某个特定位置。{w}\n我和乌尔里克背靠着背，剧烈喘息，心中升起一阵恐慌。

column5: I have an idea, [firstname].
column6: 我有个主意，[firstname]。

column5: I tilt my head toward Ulric, to signal that I'm listening.{w}\nMuch to my surprise, he sheathes his greatsword.
column6: 我朝乌尔里克偏了偏头，示意我在听。{w}\n让我大为意外的是，他收起了巨剑。

column5: Think of me as an extension of your body.\nOpen your mind — and trust me.
column6: 把我当作你身体的延伸。\n敞开心灵——相信我。

column5: I'm confused, but I nod.{w}\nThere's no time to talk, they're closing in on us.{w}\nI lunge forward, and destroy one of the suits.
column6: 我虽困惑，还是点了点头。{w}\n没时间多说了，它们正逼近我们。{w}\n我向前猛冲，摧毁了一架空甲。

column5: Now it's my turn.
column6: 现在轮到我了。

column5: The blade disappears from my hands, and appears in Ulric's.{w}\nHe uses it to slice through the suits that were closing in on him.{w}\nAs if passing a baton, the blade phases back into my hands.
column6: 刀刃从我手中消失，出现在乌尔里克手中。{w}\n他用它劈开逼近自己的空甲。{w}\n如同传递接力棒，刀刃又相位转移回我手中。

column5: I haven't fought like this in ages.\nReally gets your blood boiling, doesn't it?
column6: 我好多年没这样战斗过了。\n真让人热血沸腾，对吧？

column5: We're pressed back to back, and we keep exchanging the blade.{w}\nPhasing it from person to person as needed, we're almost one mind.{w}\nLike an intricately choreographed dance, we continue to fight.
column6: 我们紧贴着背，不断交换刀刃。{w}\n按需在彼此之间相位转移，我们几乎心意相通。{w}\n如同一支编排精妙的舞蹈，我们继续战斗。

column5: Takes me back to my time with Sovy.\nPerfect teamwork; almost unstoppable.
column6: 让我想起和索维并肩的时光。\n完美的配合；几乎无人可挡。

column5: With each passing second, we thin out the horde.{w}\nTheir numbers easily half, then they do so again, and again.{w}\nI let Ulric take the blade again, and we keep passing it back and forth.
column6: 每一秒过去，我们都在削减敌潮。{w}\n它们的数量轻松减半，接着又减半，一再减半。{w}\n我让乌尔里克再次接过刀刃，我们继续来回传递。

column5: I wish they had the courage to face us in person.\nAll they can do is hide behind their mindless slaves.
column6: 我倒希望他们有胆量亲自与我们交手。\n他们所能做的，只是躲在没有心智的奴隶背后。

column5: I could feel it. The Triumvirate was scared of us.{w}\nIn the end, all tyrants could do is cower in fright.{w}\nThey knew they had lost, and mean to buy time.
column6: 我能感觉到。三人执政团怕我们。{w}\n到头来，暴君们所能做的只有瑟瑟发抖。{w}\n他们知道自己败了，只想拖延时间。

column5: But that wasn't a luxury we were selling.\nAs the last suit of armor falls, we too, fall to our knees.{w}\nPanting heavily, we realize just how much of a fight we put up.
column6: 但这份奢侈，我们可不卖。\n最后一架空甲倒下时，我们也跪倒在地。{w}\n剧烈喘息间，我们才意识到自己打了多么艰苦的一仗。

column5: I'll never forget this moment. Not for the rest of my life.{w}\nFighting side by side with another Exodus wielder...?{w}\nIf I were The Triumvirate, I'd be very, very afraid.
column6: 我永远不会忘记这一刻。余生都不会。{w}\n与另一位流亡之刃的持有者并肩作战……？{w}\n如果我是在三人执政团，我会非常、非常害怕。

column5: It feels like an eternity before I can rise to my feet again.{w}\nBut when I do, I sheathe the blade, and look over at Ulric.{w}\nHe was staring at the stairs. Our next objective.
column6: 仿佛过了永恒那么久，我才重新站起身。{w}\n起身后，我收起刀刃，望向乌尔里克。{w}\n他正盯着楼梯。那是我们的下一个目标。

column5: If we get into a bind, let's just do the same thing.\nThat blade, and our connection, is our greatest weapon.
column6: 要是陷入困境，我们就再来一次。\n那把刀刃，以及我们之间的联结，就是我们最强的武器。

column5: I nod.
column6: 我点点头。

column5: And something tells me we'll be needing it when we face Halin.\nAre you ready to go upstairs...? He's all that stands in our way.
column6: 我有种预感，面对哈林时我们会用上它。\n你准备好上楼了吗……？他是唯一挡在我们面前的人。

column5: I nod once more.
column6: 我再次点点头。

column5: Good. Then let's go.\nRemember, if you get the chance — save him.\nI understand if you can't, but he {i}deserves{/i} freedom.
column6: 很好。那我们走吧。\n记住，如果有机会——救他。\n你做不到我也理解，但他{i}理应{/i}得到自由。

column5: It's true. Everybody deserved to be free from The Triumvirate.{w}\nBut Halin wasn't willing. We'd have to force him somehow.{w}\nAnd if we couldn't, then unfortunately, I'd have to kill him.
column6: 的确如此。每个人都该从三人执政团手中获得自由。{w}\n但哈林不愿。我们得想个办法强迫他。{w}\n要是做不到，那很遗憾，我只能杀了他。

column5: We make our way upstairs, in pursuit of Halin.{w}\nAfter what just happened — I was certain we'd win this.{w}\nWith our strength combined, nothing could stand in our way.
column6: 我们上楼，追赶哈林。{w}\n经历了刚才的事——我确信我们会赢。{w}\n我们的力量合而为一，再无任何东西能阻挡我们。

column5: The first thing I see is stairs. Lots of stairs.{w}\nThey lead upwards, and in every conceivable direction.{w}\nI know I was told there'd be lots of stairs. But this is insane.
column6: 我首先看到的是楼梯。数不清的楼梯。{w}\n它们向上延伸，通向四面八方。{w}\n我知道有人告诉过我楼梯很多。但这也太夸张了。

column5: The second thing I notice, is the complete lack of Halin.{w}\nHad he fleed up those staircases? Where could he be?{w}\nActually, I'm starting to wonder how he disappeared like that.
column6: 我注意到的第二件事，就是哈林完全不见了踪影。{w}\n他是沿着那些楼梯逃上去了吗？他能在哪儿？{w}\n其实，我开始好奇他是怎么那样凭空消失的。

column5: If he was made from the blade, could he phase around as well?{w}\nI hope that's not the case. That would prove far too tricky.{w}\nHowever, due to his loyalty, I know we'd be in for a fight.
column6: 如果他是刀刃所造，那是否也能相位转移？{w}\n希望不是如此。那会棘手得多。{w}\n不过，鉴于他的忠诚，我知道这一战在所难免。

column5: Destroyed suits of armor, and their swords, line the floor.{w}\nThis must've been the remnant of a previous fight.{w}\nPerhaps Fortaime or Pro came here before us.
column6: 地上散落着毁坏的空甲与它们的刀剑。{w}\n这一定是先前某场战斗留下的残迹。{w}\n也许福泰姆或普洛比我们先到过这里。

column5: Be careful, [firstname].\nTry not to let Halin steal the blade from you.\nRemember, we all possess the same ability.
column6: 小心，[firstname]。\n别让哈林把刀刃从你手中夺走。\n记住，我们都拥有相同的能力。

column5: Yeah — make sure to be on your guard.\nWe killed his suits, so he's probably scared.\nI wouldn't be surprised if he resorts to trickery.
column6: 是啊——务必保持警惕。\n我们杀了他的空甲，他大概怕了。\n他要是耍什么诡计，我一点也不意外。

column5: Be careful, [firstname]. This could be tricky.\nRemember that Halin can wield the blade, just like us.\nIn fact, since he was made from it, his affinity could be stronger.
column6: 小心，[firstname]。这可能很棘手。\n记住哈林能像我们一样驾驭那把刀刃。\n事实上，既然他是刀刃所造，他的亲和力或许更强。

column5: He's backed into a corner, so we don't know how he'll react.\nI wouldn't be surprised if he resorted to some sort of trap.\nA cornered man is always desperate in his final moments.
column6: 他被逼入绝境，我们不知道他会作何反应。\n他要是设下什么陷阱，我一点也不意外。\n走投无路的人，在最后时刻总会拼命。

column5: I nod. That was good advice.{w}\nI take it to heart, as we walk toward the stairs.{w}\nWe hear Halin's voice, but can't see him at all.
column6: 我点点头。那是很好的忠告。{w}\n我们朝楼梯走去，我把这话记在心上。{w}\n我们听见哈林的声音，却完全看不见他。

column5: Well then, perhaps you're stronger than I thought.\nNo matter, though — I've been waiting for a worthy opponent.\nI'll savor killing you, \"Monarch\". Every. Single. Moment.
column6: 那么，或许你们比我以为的更强。\n不过无妨——我一直在等一个配得上我的对手。\n我会细细品味杀死你的过程，“君主”。每。一。刻。

column5: That's when I finally see him. On one of the many flights of stairs.{w}\nHe's slowly making his way down, almost as if he's buying some time.{w}\nI move to meet him halfway, but suddenly, there's no need to move at all.
column6: 就在这时，我终于看见了他。在许多段楼梯中的一段上。{w}\n他缓缓走下来，几乎像是在拖延时间。{w}\n我正要上前与他会合，却突然发现根本不必移动。

column5: [firstname]! Look out...!
column6: [firstname]！小心……！

column5: Almost instinctively, I lower myself as close to the ground as possible.{w}\nFrom behind, a massive sword is swung. It came close to removing my head.{w}\nI turn around, greeted to the sight of Halin. So he {i}can{/i} move around like that.
column6: 几乎出于本能，我尽可能压低身体。{w}\n一把巨剑从身后挥来。险些削掉我的脑袋。{w}\n我转过身，映入眼帘的是哈林。原来他{i}真的{/i}能那样四处移动。

column5: Saved by your friends, as always.\nI wonder how you'd handle things on your own.\nWhat do you say — want to put that to the test...?
column6: 一如既往，被朋友们救了。\n我倒想知道你独自一人时会怎么应对。\n怎么样——想试试看吗……？

column5: Ulric steps forward, interrupting before I can respond.
column6: 我还没来得及回答，乌尔里克便上前打断。

column5: We don't have time for your games, Halin.\nWe'll give you one chance. Surrender, or die.
column6: 我们没时间陪你玩把戏，哈林。\n我们给你一次机会。投降，或者死。

column5: And who says {i}you{/i} get to call the shots?\nRemember, I exist to manifest The Triumvirate's will.\nAnd right now — what they want — is to see you all dead.
column6: 谁说{i}你们{/i}能发号施令？\n记住，我存在的意义就是彰显三人执政团的意志。\n而此刻——他们所愿的——就是看你们全都死掉。

column5: Halin draws another sword, holding out two large blades.
column6: 哈林又拔出一把剑，手持两柄巨刃。

column5: I've never let them down, and I don't plan on starting.\nYou think you're special? That you're here to seize your destiny?\nNo. You're nothing more than another insect for me to crush.
column6: 我从未让他们失望过，也不打算破例。\n你以为自己很特别？以为你来这是为了夺取天命？\n不。你不过是我又要碾死的一只虫子。

column5: You may have made it farther than most, but it doesn't matter.\nEven atop the highest mountain, an insect is still an insect.\nA being that exists for one purpose — to be exterminated.
column6: 你或许比大多数人走得更远，但这无关紧要。\n即便身处最高的山巅，虫子终究是虫子。\n一种只为某个目的而存在的生物——被消灭。

column5: He charges toward me, and I do the same.{w}\nPulling out The Blade of Exodus, our swords clash as we meet.{w}\nThey meet again, and again — the echo filling the room as we fight.
column6: 他朝我冲来，我也迎了上去。{w}\n我拔出流亡之刃，两剑相接，我们正面交锋。{w}\n剑锋一次次相击——交锋声中，回响充满了整个房间。

column5: His strength is astounding, as well as his speed.{w}\nI've never seen a man fight with two swords quite so gracefully.{w}\nHe tries to trick me, with fake swings, and sudden movements.
column6: 他的力量惊人，速度亦然。{w}\n我从未见过有人双手使剑能有这般优雅。{w}\n他试图用虚招和突然的变招来迷惑我。

column5: But he'll have to try harder than that. I counter him with ease.{w}\nThis dance continues, and we show no signs of tiring out.{w}\nAt this rate, death would come to whoever slipped up first.
column6: 但他还得再加把劲。我轻松地化解了他的攻势。{w}\n这共舞持续着，我们都没有疲态。{w}\n照这样下去，谁先失手，谁就会死。

column5: But I can't slip up. I have to win, and take down The Triumvirate.{w}\nThis world belonged to {i}me{/i}. I was the rightful heir to the throne.{w}\nHalin was just a lackey to some power hungry group of three.
column6: 但我不能失手。我必须赢，必须推翻三人执政团。{w}\n这个世界本就属于{i}我{/i}。我是王位的合法继承人。{w}\n哈林不过是那三个贪权者的走狗。

column5: If there was any justice in the world, then I would prevail.{w}\nPerhaps I let that get to my head. This allows Halin to land a blow.{w}\nThrusting his blade into my shoulder, he twists it, then pulls it out.
column6: 若这世上还有公道，那我必胜。{w}\n也许我因此冲昏了头。这让哈林抓住机会命中一剑。{w}\n他把剑刺进我的肩膀，拧转一下，又拔了出来。

column5: It was a wound that would prove to be harmless, in the long run.{w}\nBut the pain is so intense, all I can do is stand there, stiff and motionless.{w}\nMy blood drips to the floor, and I take a few steps back, losing balance.
column6: 长远来看，这伤口算不上大碍。{w}\n但疼痛如此剧烈，我只能僵立原地，动弹不得。{w}\n鲜血滴落在地，我踉跄后退几步，失去了平衡。

column5: [firstname]...!
column6: [firstname]……！

column5: Sovy lunges forward, and pushes me to the ground.{w}\nPhasing the blade into his hands, he blocks Halin's next attack.{w}\nI bleed on the floor as I watch Sovy fight his former Apprentice.
column6: 索维冲上前，把我推倒在地。{w}\n他将刀刃相位转移到手中，挡下哈林接下来的攻击。{w}\n我躺在地上流血，看着索维与他昔日的学徒交手。

column5: There's something different about you, Sovy.\nWhere was this passion when {i}we{/i} worked together...?
column6: 你有些不一样了，索维。\n{i}我们{/i}共事的时候，这份热情去哪了……？

column5: Swords continue to clash, and Halin is right.{w}\nI've never seen Sovy quite so determined.
column6: 刀剑继续相交，哈林说得没错。{w}\n我从未见过索维如此决绝。

column5: The Triumvirate doesn't allow passion, Halin. They take everything away. \nThey bleed you dry, and offer nothing in return. Nothing but empty words!\nThe Rebellion gave me a place in this world. I belong to them, now!
column6: 三人执政团不容许热情，哈林。他们会夺走一切。\n他们榨干你，却什么也不给。只有空话！\n是反抗军给了我在这世上的位置。我现在属于他们！

column5: You mean they seduced you with flights of fancy.\nYou honestly believe that {i}he{/i} is our rightful ruler...?
column6: 你是说，他们用那些天花乱坠的幻想诱惑了你。\n你真的相信{i}他{/i}是我们合法的统治者……？

column5: You mean they seduced you with flights of fancy.\nYou honestly believe that {i}she{/i} is our rightful ruler...?
column6: 你是说，他们用那些天花乱坠的幻想诱惑了你。\n你真的相信{i}她{/i}是我们合法的统治者……？

column5: Sovy nods.
column6: 索维点点头。

column5: Without a doubt. I'd give my {i}life{/i} for [firstname]....\nI know the truth of the Spirit Realm. The Triumvirate told me.\nThis isn't some dream, or fantasy. They told me themselves...!
column6: 毫无疑问。我愿为[firstname]献出{i}生命{/i}……\n我知道灵界的真相。是三人执政团亲口告诉我的。\n这不是什么梦，也不是幻想。是他们亲口说的……！

column5: Halin seems surprised, as if he still trusts Sovy.
column6: 哈林似乎很惊讶，仿佛他仍然信任着索维。

column5: You mean...?
column6: 你是说……？

column5: Yes. That's what they told me before we left for Mazeo.\nIt's why I didn't kill The Monarch when I had the chance.\nI told myself I'd never harm those in charge of this world.
column6: 是的。那是我们出发去马泽奥之前，他们告诉我的。\n所以我才没有在有机会时杀掉君主。\n我告诉自己，绝不伤害执掌这个世界的人。

column5: That's what separates the both of us, Halin.\nMy loyalty is to Alestia. {i}Yours{/i} is to The Triumvirate.\nThey made you a slave, with no choice but to obey.
column6: 这就是我们两人的区别，哈林。\n我忠于阿莱斯蒂亚。{i}你{/i}忠于三人执政团。\n他们把你变成了奴隶，让你别无选择，只能服从。

column5: No. I {i}want{/i} to serve them...!\nYour faith was challenged, and {i}you{/i} gave up.\nI'm not that weak. I stand tall, and remain in line.
column6: 不。我{i}想{/i}效忠他们……！\n你的信念受到挑战，于是{i}你{/i}放弃了。\n我没那么软弱。我挺直腰杆，恪守本分。

column5: Sovy lowers the blade, signalling his intent to stop fighting.
column6: 索维放下刀刃，示意自己无意再战。

column5: Then let [firstname] remove the curse they've put on you.\nIf you still want to serve them, then we can continue to fight.\nAnd if not — then you'll realize that you were wrong all along.
column6: 那就让[firstname]解除他们加在你身上的诅咒。\n如果你仍想效忠他们，我们就继续打。\n若不然——你就会明白，你一直都错了。

column5: Halin reacts with anger to that last part, and charges toward Sovy.{w}\nThey're fighting again. Just when things started to turn around.
column6: 哈林对最后那句话勃然大怒，朝索维冲去。{w}\n他们又打起来了。就在局势刚有转机的时候。

column5: No — I'm not wrong. I'll never give up, Sovy. Never!\nIf you want to pay with your life, then I'll accept that toll.\nBut know this. It brings me no pleasure to—
column6: 不——我没错。我绝不放弃，索维。绝不！\n既然你想用性命来付账，那我就收下这份代价。\n但你要知道。这并非我所愿——

column5: And a moment later, Sovy thrusts the blade through Halin's gut.{w}\nSovy looks horrified, as he harms his former Apprentice, and friend.{w}\nNo turning back. This was the exact moment his defection was complete.
column6: 片刻之后，索维把刀刃刺进了哈林的腹部。{w}\n伤到自己昔日的学徒兼朋友，索维一脸骇然。{w}\n再无回头路。就在这一刻，他的叛离彻底完成。

column5: S-Sovy...?
Halin grunts in pain as Sovy removes the blade.{w}\nA horrific wound, but I don't think it would be enough.{w}\nCreated from the blade, Halin was surely resilient.
column6: 索维拔出刀刃，哈林痛得闷哼出声。{w}\n好可怕的伤口，但我觉得这还不够。{w}\n既然由刀刃所造，哈林一定很顽强。

column5: Halin, I'm sorry...\nI — I didn't want it to be this way...!
column6: 哈林，对不起……\n我——我不想变成这样……！

column5: I can hear such sadness in his voice. He's conflicted.{w}\nLooking down at the floor, Sovy shakes as he watches Halin bleed out.{w}\nA moment later, he falls forward, and Sovy catches him in his arms.
column6: 我能听出他声音里的悲伤。他内心挣扎。{w}\n索维低头看着地面，望着哈林流血不止，浑身发颤。{w}\n片刻之后，哈林向前倒下，索维用双臂接住了他。

column5: On the verge of tears, Sovy turns Halin around.{w}\nLowering him to the ground, he puts him in a strong chokehold.{w}\nHalin struggles, trying to escape, but the wound rendered him too weak.
column6: 索维几乎要落泪，把哈林转过身来。{w}\n他将哈林放到地上，牢牢勒住他的脖颈。{w}\n哈林挣扎着想挣脱，但伤势让他太过虚弱。

column5: [firstname]...! Do something!\nI don't care what it is — just do it!
column6: [firstname]……！做点什么！\n我不管是什么——快动手！

column5: I look over at Ulric, and he watches in shock.{w}\nI know that wound wouldn't kill Halin. Just temporarily incapacitate him.{w}\nSovy must've known. But the sight, and what he did, was still too much for him.
column6: 我看向乌尔里克，他震惊地望着这一切。{w}\n我知道那伤杀不死哈林，只会让他暂时失去行动力。{w}\n索维一定也清楚。但眼前的景象，以及自己所做的，仍让他难以承受。

column5: There's no way Halin could fight back right now.{w}\nI could kill him with no difficulty at all. But I could also save him.{w}\nIf I removed the curse on his mind, maybe he'd serve our cause instead.
column6: 哈林此刻绝无可能反击。{w}\n我可以毫不费力地杀了他，但也能救他。{w}\n若我解除他脑中的诅咒，或许他会转而为我们的事业效力。

column5: But was that worth the risk...?{w}\nSomething tells me I don't have much time to decide.{w}\nIf Sovy held him like that for too long, he'd be dead for sure.
column6: 但这值得冒险吗……？{w}\n我有种预感，没多少时间让我犹豫了。{w}\n要是索维那样勒他太久，他必死无疑。

column5: [firstname]...!
column6: [firstname]……！

column5: Ulric lunges forward, and pushes me to the ground.{w}\nPhasing the blade into his hands, he blocks Halin's next attack.{w}\nI bleed on the floor as I watch Ulric fight The Triumvirate's right hand.
column6: 乌尔里克冲上前，把我推倒在地。{w}\n他将刀刃相位转移到手中，挡下哈林接下来的攻击。{w}\n我躺在地上流血，看着乌尔里克与三人执政团的右手交手。

column5: Hmm. You're certainly stronger than Sovy.\nIt's a shame that you defected. I could use you.
column6: 唔。你确实比索维强。\n你叛离了，真是可惜。我本可以用你。

column5: Defected? No. I simply chose the right path.\nAnd you can do that too, Halin. It's not too late.
column6: 叛离？不。我只是选择了正确的路。\n你也可以这么做，哈林。还不算晚。

column5: Halin laughs, and they continue to fight.{w}\nSwords clash, but Ulric clearly has the edge.
column6: 哈林大笑，两人继续交手。{w}\n刀剑相交，但乌尔里克明显占了上风。

column5: There's no passion in serving The Triumvirate.\nThey take everything away. They bleed you dry.\nAnd what's worse, they give nothing in return.
column6: 效忠三人执政团毫无热情可言。\n他们会夺走一切。他们榨干你。\n更糟的是，他们什么回报都不给。

column5: The Rebellion gave me everything I needed.\nA family. A home. A place in this world.\nI belong to them now, and that's final.
column6: 反抗军给了我所需的一切。\n一个家。一个归宿。在这世上的一席之地。\n我现在属于他们，仅此而已。

column5: Halin shakes his head.
column6: 哈林摇摇头。

column5: You're a fool. They seduce you with flights of fancy.\nYou ran to the {i}first{/i} group that made you feel a sense of purpose.\nDo you honestly think that {i}he{/i} is the rightful ruler of Alestia...?
column6: 你是个蠢货。他们用天花乱坠的幻想诱惑你。\n你投向了{i}第一个{/i}让你感到有意义的团体。\n你真的相信{i}他{/i}是阿莱斯蒂亚合法的统治者……？

column5: You're a fool. They seduce you with flights of fancy.\nYou ran to the first group that made you feel a sense of purpose.\nDo you honestly think that {i}she{/i} is the rightful ruler of Alestia...?
column6: 你是个蠢货。他们用天花乱坠的幻想诱惑你。\n你投向了第一个让你感到有意义的团体。\n你真的相信{i}她{/i}是阿莱斯蒂亚合法的统治者……？

column5: Ulric nods.
column6: 乌尔里克点点头。

column5: Without a doubt. I'd give my life for [firstname].\nThe truth of the Spirit Realm only proves that I'm correct.\nThey told Sovy, and look at what happened. Think, Halin.
column6: 毫无疑问。我愿为[firstname]献出生命。\n灵界的真相恰恰证明我是对的。\n他们告诉过索维，看看结果如何。想一想，哈林。

column5: I'm not weak. My loyalty was just different from yours.\nWhile I want to serve Alestia, you want to serve The Triumvirate.\nBut they made you that way. We can change you, if you'll let us.
column6: 我不软弱。我的忠诚只是与你不同。\n我想效忠阿莱斯蒂亚，你却想效忠三人执政团。\n但那是他们把你塑造成这样的。只要你愿意，我们就能改变你。

column5: They continue to fight, as they argue with one another.
column6: 他们一边争论，一边继续交手。

column5: No. I {i}want{/i} to serve them! \nYou run away, while I stand tall, and remain in line.\nHow can you say you're not weak, after what you've done?
column6: 不。我{i}想{/i}效忠他们！\n你只会逃跑，而我都挺直腰杆，恪守本分。\n做了那些事之后，你怎么还敢说自己不软弱？

column5: Ulric lowers his sword, signalling his intent to stop fighting.
column6: 乌尔里克放下剑，示意自己无意再战。

column5: Are you willing to bet on that...?
column6: 你愿意为此赌一把吗……？

column5: Hmm...
Halin still holds his swords up, to guard himself.
column6: 哈林仍举着双剑，警惕地护住自己。

column5: Let [firstname] remove the curse that they put on you.\nIf you still want to serve them, then we can continue to fight.\nAnd if not — then you'll realize that you were wrong all along.
column6: 那就让[firstname]解除他们加在你身上的诅咒。\n如果你仍想效忠他们，我们就继续打。\n若不然——你就会明白，你一直都错了。

column5: No... I can't...
column6: 不……我做不到……

column5: Halin looks scared, like he's fighting with himself.{w}\nThat moment of hesitation is all that Ulric needs.{w}\nHe uses the pommel of his sword as a weapon.
column6: 哈林面露恐惧，仿佛在与自己搏斗。{w}\n那一瞬间的犹豫，对乌尔里克来说已然足够。{w}\n他以剑柄为武器。

column5: Smashing it into Halin's head, he knocks him into a daze.{w}\nHe falls forward, but Ulric catches him in his arms.
column6: 剑柄狠狠砸在哈林头上，将他击得神志恍惚。{w}\n他向前倒下，乌尔里克用双臂接住了他。

column5: [firstname], do it now...!\nI don't care what it is — just do it!
column6: [firstname]，现在就动手……！\n我不管是什么——快动手！

column5: He turns Halin around, and lowers him to his knees.{w}\nPutting him into a chokehold, he tries to break free, but he's too weak.{w}\nBlood drips down his face. Ulric clearly wasn't holding back.
column6: 他把哈林转过身，按得他跪在地上。{w}\n他勒住哈林的脖颈，哈林想挣脱，却太虚弱了。{w}\n鲜血顺着他的脸滴落。乌尔里克显然没有留情。

column5: There's no way Halin could fight back right now.{w}\nI could kill him with no difficulty at all. But I could also save him.{w}\nIf I removed the curse on his mind, maybe he'd serve our cause instead.
column6: 哈林此刻绝无可能反击。{w}\n我可以毫不费力地杀了他，但也能救他。{w}\n若我解除他脑中的诅咒，或许他会转而为我们的事业效力。

column5: But was that worth the risk...?{w}\nSomething tells me I don't have much time to decide.{w}\nIf Ulric held him like that for too long, he'd be dead for sure.
column6: 但这值得冒险吗……？{w}\n我有种预感，没多少时间让我犹豫了。{w}\n要是乌尔里克那样勒他太久，他必死无疑。

column5: I have to do it. Killing Halin was the only right choice in this situation.{w}\nWith free will, Halin could act any way he wanted. I know what that would mean.{w}\nIt would just confirm his allegiance to his Masters, and make him even stronger.
column6: 我必须动手。在这种情况下，杀掉哈林是唯一正确的选择。{w}\n若他拥有自由意志，便能随心所欲地行动。我知道那意味着什么。{w}\n那只会坐实他对主子的忠诚，让他变得更强。

column5: Even if it was born from denial, we couldn't afford it right now.{w}\nWe needed to get to The Triumvirate's chambers, and end this.{w}\nI phase the blade back into my hand, and slowly stand up.
column6: 即便这念头源于自欺，我们此刻也承担不起。{w}\n我们必须抵达三人执政团的房间，了结这一切。{w}\n我将刀刃相位转移回手中，缓缓站起。

column5: I tell Sovy to let go, and move back. He obeys without hesitation.{w}\nHalin is on his knees, crying, and staring over in my direction.{w}\nI will show him no mercy, for it wasn't something he deserved.
column6: 我叫索维松手后退。他毫不迟疑地照做。{w}\n哈林跪在地上，哭喊着，朝我的方向望来。{w}\n我不会对他施以仁慈，因为他不配。

column5: I raise my blade in the air, and the suits of armor on the floor start to shake.{w}\nBut that's not what I was after. A moment later, Sovy and Ulric gasp softly.{w}\nAll of their swords slowly rise. Hundreds of them float in the air.
column6: 我高举刀刃，地上的空甲开始颤动。{w}\n但那并非我的目标。片刻之后，索维和乌尔里克轻轻倒吸一口气。{w}\n它们所有的剑缓缓升起。数百把剑悬浮在空中。

column5: I tell Ulric to let go, and move back. He obeys without hesitation.{w}\nHalin is on his knees, crying, and staring over in my direction.{w}\nI will show him no mercy, for it wasn't something he deserved.

column5: And I immediately turn them toward Halin.{w}\nHe keeps staring at me. If he had any last words, he chose to stay silent.{w}\nWith a snap of my fingers, every single sword pierces through him at once.
column6: 我立刻把它们转向哈林。{w}\n他依旧盯着我。若他有任何遗言，他选择沉默。{w}\n我打了个响指，每一把剑同时贯穿了他。

column5: He would've let out a scream, if he was capable. But he's not.{w}\nHis head slumps down, and he stares at the blades in his body.{w}\nTrying to pull them out, he realizes very fast that he's too weak.
column6: 若他还能，他定会惨叫出声。但他不能。{w}\n他的头垂了下来，盯着插在身上的刀刃。{w}\n他想把它们拔出，却很快意识到自己太过虚弱。

column5: But this wasn't enough to satisfy me. Halin needed to suffer.{w}\nFor every Rebel he killed, I would make him feel {i}all{/i} of my fury.{w}\nHe was created by the blade, so I use that fact against him.
column6: 但这还不足以让我满足。哈林必须受苦。{w}\n他每杀一名反抗军，我就要让他感受我{i}全部{/i}的怒火。{w}\n他是刀刃所造，我便利用这一点来对付他。

column5: If I could control the blade, then I could easily control him as well.{w}\nI hold The Blade of Exodus toward him, and make it enact my will.{w}\nHalin's armor starts to crack, and I use it to crush his body.
column6: 若我能操控刀刃，那也能轻易操控他。{w}\n我把流亡之刃指向他，让它执行我的意志。{w}\n哈林的甲胄开始开裂，我用它来挤压他的身体。

column5: I make it squeeze so tight around him, that I hear his bones crack.{w}\nThe constriction of his body is so grotesque, but I don't let up until the end.{w}\nWhen I'm done with him, he slumps over, crushed and pierced with swords.
column6: 我让它紧紧箍住他，紧得我听见他骨骼碎裂的声音。{w}\n那躯体被挤压的模样如此可怖，但我一刻也不松懈。{w}\n等我收手时，他已瘫倒下去，被压碎，被刀剑刺穿。

column5: I had to liberate Halin. I had to let him survive, and give him a chance.{w}\nIf he still chose to oppose us, then we could execute him after the war.{w}\nBut as long as his conversion was a possiblity, I had to take a chance.
column6: 我必须解放哈林。我必须让他活下来，给他一个机会。{w}\n若他仍选择与我们为敌，那我们可以在战后处决他。{w}\n但只要他还有转化的可能，我就必须赌一把。

column5: I tell Sovy to release the chokehold, but hold Halin in place.{w}\nHe obeys without hesitation, and I slowly make my way over to him.{w}\nPressing the blade against Halin's chest, I ask it to give him his freedom.
column6: 我叫索维松开锁喉，但按紧哈林。{w}\n他毫不迟疑地照做，我缓缓走向哈林。{w}\n我把刀刃抵在哈林胸口，请它赐予他自由。

column5: I tell Ulric to release the chokehold, but hold Halin in place.{w}\nHe obeys without hesitation, and I slowly make my way over to him.{w}\nPressing the blade against Halin's chest, I ask it to give him his freedom.
column6: 我叫乌尔里克松开锁喉，但按紧哈林。{w}\n他毫不迟疑地照做，我缓缓走向哈林。{w}\n我把刀刃抵在哈林胸口，请它赐予他自由。

column5: A few seconds later, Halin falls to the ground, unconscious.{w}\nI have him carried over to a safe spot, where he could recover in silence.{w}\nIf, and when, he woke up — I hoped that it would be as a new, smarter man.
column6: 几秒之后，哈林失去意识，倒在地上。{w}\n我吩咐把他抬到一处安全的地方，好让他静静地恢复。{w}\n若他醒来——我希望那会是一个崭新的、更明智的人。

column5: With that out of the way, we had to make our way up those stairs.{w}\nWithin a few more minutes, I'd be face to face with our enemy.{w}\nIt was time to rise to the challenge, and change this world.
column6: 此事既了，我们得继续登上那些楼梯。{w}\n再过几分钟，我就要与我们的敌人正面相对。{w}\n是时候迎接挑战，改变这个世界了。

column5: You know what...? I'll stay behind.\nPro and Fortaime should be at the atrium any minute, now.\nI want to make sure I'm there to greet them, and fill them in.
column6: 你知道吗……？我留下来吧。\n普洛和福泰姆随时都该到中庭了。\n我想确保自己在那儿迎接他们，把事情告诉他们。

column5: Are you sure...?
column6: 你确定吗……？

column5: Yeah. It's not my place to face The Triumvirate. Not again.\nThis fight belongs to the both of you, so go and see it through.
column6: 嗯。面对三人执政团，不该是我。不能再是我。\n这一战属于你们两人，去吧，把它了结。

column5: We both nod at him, as he makes his way back to the atrium.{w}\nOn his way out, he picks a sword up from the ground.{w}\nSovy scoffs, and does the same thing soon after.
column6: 他朝中庭走去，我们两人都向他点头。{w}\n离开时，他从地上捡起一把剑。{w}\n索维嗤笑一声，随后也照做了。

column5: A good idea, actually.\nSomething tells me we'll be fighting even more.\nSay — can you do me one favor before we head up?
column6: 这主意其实不错。\n我有种预感，接下来还要打更多。\n对了——上去之前，能帮我一个忙吗？

column5: I nod.
column6: 我点点头。

column5: Here. Just trust me.
column6: 来。相信我便是。

column5: He reaches behind me, and adjusts my scabbard.{w}\nI'm not sure why, but he switches it to the other side.{w}\nI'm left handed, so this would only make things harder.
column6: 他伸手到我背后，调整我的剑鞘。{w}\n我不明白为什么，但他把它换到了另一侧。{w}\n我是左撇子，这只会让事情更难办。

column5: He reaches behind me, and adjusts my scabbard.{w}\nI'm not sure why, but he switches it to the other side.{w}\nI'm not left handed, so that only made things awkward.
column6: 他伸手到我背后，调整我的剑鞘。{w}\n我不明白为什么，但他把它换到了另一侧。{w}\n我不是左撇子，这只会让事情变得别扭。

column5: But I choose to trust him.
column6: 但我选择相信他。

column5: Thank you.
column6: 谢谢你。

column5: And a second later, we're making our way up the stairs.{w}\nAll we had to do was dethrone The Triumvirate. Simple enough.{w}\nAfter that, I'd meet my friends in the atrium. At least, the ones that survived.

column5: But I choose to trust him, as I always have.
column6: 但我选择相信他，一如我向来所做。

column5: Thank you.
column6: 谢谢你。
